_readme: THE APPLE PROVISIONING REGISTER — the ONE declared capability list per app, and what each capability
means on the Apple side. O-STAMP-APPLE-PROVISIONING-MANUAL; the structure it keeps is [ADR 088].
READ BY:
tooling/ci/assert-apple-entitlements.mjs  (ci.yml, no credentials) — every app's
ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements carries EXACTLY the keys this file derives for it, and the
Xcode project points at that file. ⏱ 2026-09-18: and every macOS entitlements file named in
`macosEntitlementFiles` carries EXACTLY its base sandbox keys plus the macOS keys the
capability list derives, and the macOS Xcode project names exactly that set of files.
tooling/ops/provision-apple.mjs  (a laptop command, the vault's ASC key) — provisions the
API-WRITABLE part of an app's App ID from this list, REFUSES on the part the API cannot write,
mints the App Store profiles after the capabilities settle, and with --check compares the
LIVE profile's entitlements against this list and against Runner.entitlements.
Both go through tooling/ci/apple-provisioning.mjs, so the two cannot disagree about what a
declared capability requires.
THE API BOUNDARY IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-09-16, against the live account, see ADR 088 §6):
`apiWritable: true` means POST /v1/bundleIdCapabilities was observed to accept this capability for
an APP. `false` means it was refused, OR it is accepted only in a shape that is WRONG for an app —
APPLE_ID_AUTH is writable solely as PRIMARY_APP_CONSENT, which would make the app its own consent
anchor and silently hand every shared user a second identity. So for an app, Sign in with Apple is
the portal grouping step, and this file says so.
`profileKey` is the entitlement Apple writes into an App Store profile when the App ID carries the
capability — READ BACK from profiles JWVU72A2N6 and 26RV2N2Y4L on 2026-09-16. IN_APP_PURCHASE
writes none. `entitlementKey` is what the app's own Runner.entitlements must carry; it is null for
APPLE_ID_AUTH because every target signs in through the OAuth redirect and the one Services ID
(packages/auth_supabase/lib/src/supabase_auth_repository.dart, ADR 088 §4): the capability is on the
App ID for the consent GROUP, not for a native API the app calls. An app that adopts the native
AuthenticationServices flow changes this row, and the guard then demands the key.
⏱ 2026-09-18 · O-STAMP-APPLE-MACOS-ENTITLEMENTS. `entitlementKey` takes the same three shapes
`profileKey` does: null, a STRING meaning the same key on iOS AND macOS, or `{ ios, macos }` with
either side null. DECLARED_AGE_RANGE is the reason the object form exists: its only consumer,
packages/platform_storage/ios/nikatru_platform_storage/Sources/nikatru_platform_storage/
AgeSignalsPlugin.swift, is iOS-only (there is no macos/ twin), so the macOS files must NOT
carry it. Left a plain string, the key would now be demanded on macOS too — which is why that row
moved to the object form in the same change as this paragraph.

anchor.why: The Sign in with Apple consent anchor. Ships no app. Every app's App ID is grouped under it (ADR 088 §2). The ONLY App ID in the team allowed to read back PRIMARY_APP_CONSENT — which is how a RELATED_APP_CONSENT read-back is known to point here: the API does not say which primary an App ID is related to, so the script also asserts the team has exactly one primary and that it is this one.

protected.why: Live, hand-grouped, or baked into the APPLE_PROVISIONING_PROFILES_BASE64 secret. provision-apple.mjs refuses to delete, re-create, re-group or re-mint any of these even with --apply, and says what it would have done instead. Re-minting a protected profile breaks the release lane until the secret is re-set, which is an owner step.

_retired_why: O-APPLE-RESOURCE-IDS-IN-COMMENTS. App Store Connect resource ids that were live once and are not now, kept here
so an id read in an old log or PR still resolves to what it was. This register is the ONLY tracked home of an
Apple resource id: assert-apple-entitlements.mjs refuses any id from this file (anchor, protected, apps, retired)
written as a literal in tooling/ci/**/*.mjs, where a comment naming one goes stale the day it is re-minted.
`retiredOn` comes from git history; `unknown` where no commit records the day, never a guess.

retired.why: The UNIVERSAL App ID for com.nikatru.subly. Deleted when the package identifier moved to com.nikatru.subscriptiontracker (ADR 067's slug rename); an App ID is not renamable. Recorded deleted in a7b92d8e (#576).
The IOS_APP_STORE profile against YZGQND6Z9C. A profile is issued against one App ID, so it was deleted with it. Recorded deleted in a7b92d8e (#576).
The MAC_APP_STORE profile against YZGQND6Z9C, deleted with it. Recorded deleted in a7b92d8e (#576).

The UNIVERSAL App ID for com.nikatru.subscriptiontracker minted in a7b92d8e (#576). Superseded by apps.subscriptiontracker.resourceId, first recorded in 500af608 (#780) on 2026-09-16; an identifier holds one App ID, so it was gone by then. No commit records the deletion day.
The IOS_APP_STORE profile against W5XX7RJ4WQ, minted in a7b92d8e (#576). Superseded by protected.profiles, first recorded in 500af608 (#780) on 2026-09-16. No commit records the deletion day.
The MAC_APP_STORE profile against W5XX7RJ4WQ, minted in a7b92d8e (#576). Superseded by protected.profiles, first recorded in 500af608 (#780) on 2026-09-16. No commit records the deletion day.

APPLE_ID_AUTH.portalStep: developer.apple.com → Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles → Identifiers → {identifier} → tick Sign In with Apple → Edit → choose 'Group with an existing primary App ID' → com.nikatru.platform → Save → Confirm. The API refuses RELATED_APP_CONSENT on write (ADR 088 §6); writing PRIMARY_APP_CONSENT instead would split every shared user's identity.

DECLARED_AGE_RANGE.portalStep: developer.apple.com → Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles → Identifiers → {identifier} → Capabilities → tick Declared Age Range → Save → Confirm. The API refuses DECLARED_AGE_RANGE as a capabilityType on write (ADR 088 §6).

_why: ⏱ 2026-09-18 · O-STAMP-APPLE-MACOS-ENTITLEMENTS. The BASE App Sandbox keys of each macOS
entitlements file, keyed by the path the macOS Xcode project's CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS names. Every
app shares Flutter's sandbox base, so this block is global; an app's DECLARED capabilities add their
macOS keys on top (the `macos` side of each `entitlementKey`). These are App Sandbox keys, NOT App ID
capabilities: nothing here needs a portal step, and nothing here touches a profile.
WHY EACH KEY IS HERE — the history both files carried as comments, kept because the files may now be
rewritten from this block and a rewrite would drop a comment:
· com.apple.security.network.client is REQUIRED FOR THE APP TO WORK AT ALL ON macOS, and it was
missing from BOTH files until 2026-08-17. Under App Sandbox an outbound socket needs it explicitly;
without it every request to Supabase and to the Workers fails at the OS layer, in a RELEASE build
only, on the one platform this repo cannot build locally to notice. Both files had been stock
· com.apple.security.network.server (DebugProfile only) is Flutter's debug VM service listening
locally. It does NOT grant outbound calls — its presence is why the missing network.client went
unnoticed in debug for so long.
· com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit (DebugProfile only) is the Dart VM's JIT in a debug build.
· com.apple.security.app-sandbox is the Mac App Store's requirement for every app.
